propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui animae famuli tui Gregorii aeternae beatitudinis praemia
contulisti: concede propitius; ut, qui peccatorum nostrorum pondere
premimur, ejus apud te precibus sublevemur. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum
Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Annue nobis, quaesumus, Domine: ut II intercession e beati Gregorii haec
nobis prosit oblatio, quam immolando totius mundi tribuisti relaxari
delicta. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et
regnat in unitate.

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

The 12 March Mass begins on leaf n570, printed p. 562, headed `XII. St. GREGORY, p. c.`, and its Secret and Postcommunion stand at the head of leaf n571, printed p. 563, under the running head `17th AND 19th MARCH`. The Secret is set with no Latin cue; it answers `Annue nobis, quaesumus`. A bounded page-image collation confirms the complete target identity. For All Souls this is the first 2-November form only; the second and third forms remain quarantined for substantive wording differences.

translations.text: Grant, we beseech thee, O Lord, by the intercession of blessed Gregory, that this sacrifice may be beneficial to us, by the offering of which thou hast been pleased to cancel the sins of the world. Thro'.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Deus, qui beatum Gregorium Pontificem Sanctorum tuorum meritis coaequasti:
concede propitius; ut, qui commemorationis ejus festa percolimus, vitae
quoque imitemur exempla. Per Dominum.

Same leaf as the Secret above. Latin cue `Deus, qui.`, answering `Deus, qui beatum Gregorium`. A bounded page-image collation confirms the complete target identity.
